summary: Read-only audit of three untouched game areas, each finding adversarially verified against the code

confirmed.title: Net lifetime earnings ignores stall money that was carried out and banked
confirmed.where: runEarnings, about line 20061 (read by addProgress ~20081 and the Mainframe card ~33203)
confirmed.steps: Go up with an empty backpack. Loot about $3,000. Walk to THE PEDDLER, press 1 (SELL BACKPACK): the panel says the $1,650 rides with you. Extract. The outcome card prints 'Stall money carried out: $1,650, banked.' and your Credits rise by $1,650, but the Mainframe's 'Net lifetime earnings' card (its own text: 'everything you have extracted, minus everything you carried in') does not move, because the haul it sums is the bag, which the stall emptied. Pack $500 of your own kit first and the same run makes the figure FALL by $500 on a raid that banked $1,650. The run record already carries the stall total as rec.pedSold (line ~20782), and it is banked only on an extraction (line ~20438), so it is the same money.
confirmed.test: Inside the closure: runEarnings({outcome:'extract',haul:0,carriedIn:0,pedSold:1650}) must equal 1650; on the current build it returns 0. Control: runEarnings({outcome:'extract',haul:520,carriedIn:0,pedSold:0}) returns 520 on both builds, and runEarnings({outcome:'dead',haul:0,carriedIn:0,pedSold:1650}) returns 0 on both (stall money dies where you fall). End-to-end arm: stage a raid on the fixture, set G.bag=[], G.carriedIn=0, G.pedCarry=G.pedSold=G.tel.pedSold=1650, note P.netEarn and P.credits, call endRaid('extract'): P.credits rises 1650 on both builds; P.netEarn rises 1650 only after the fix.

verdict.reason: Confirmed in C:\claudecode\dark raiders\dark_raiders.html (v15.80), every step against the live code. (1) Line 20061 is verbatim `function runEarnings(rec){ return ((rec.outcome==='extract')?(rec.haul||0):0)-(rec.carriedIn||0); }`; its only readers are netEarnFromLog (20062) and addProgress line 20081 `P.netEarn=(P.netEarn||0)+runEarnings(rec);`, which commitRun (19741-19744) calls on pendingRun; the Mainframe card at 33203-33204 prints P.netEarn under the text 'everything you have extracted, minus everything you carried in'. (2) haul is the backpack at raid end only: endRaid line 20149 `var T=G.tel,haul=0,i;` then `for(i=0;i<G.bag.length;i++) haul+=ival(G.bag[i]);`. (3) pedSellAll (9522-9534) empties the sold items with `G.bag=kept;` and adds the same `tot` to both counters: `G.pedCarry=(G.pedCarry||0)+tot; G.pedSold=(G.pedSold||0)+tot; if(G.tel) G.tel.pedSold=G.pedSold;`. G.pedCarry has no other writer (9562 refuses to spend it at the stall), so pedCarry equals pedSold at raid end; both start fresh with G each raid. (4) It is banked only on the extract branch, line 20438 `if(G.pedCarry&&!G.sim){ P.credits+=G.pedCarry; }`, and the card says so at 20371 'Stall money carried out: ... banked.' (5) The record carries the number: 20763-20764 `haul:haul, ... carriedIn:G.carriedIn||0` and 20782 `pedSold:T.pedSold||0`. (6) startRaid line 10945 `G.carriedIn=bagValue();`, so $500 of own kit sold at the stall then extracted gives runEarnings 0-500 = -500 on a run that raised Credits: the 'falls by $500' step is real. No comment or ruling excludes stall money; the v10.27 comment at 20077 says 'Everything extracted minus everything carried in'. This is a lifetime counter, not a dial, so not balance; no player text or TXSHIP key is touched. The proposed fix is correct and safe for old records (pedSold||0; netEarnFromLog runs once at 2798 only for profiles without the counter). Note: the same finding with the same fix is already logged real in tools/handoff/audit-wvw8zcvyw.json, and no draft in tools/handoff (d*/cm*/a*) has queued it; the live line is unchanged, so it is still open.

confirmed.title: Wirt's gamble history prints the table value, not what the item is worth or sells for
confirmed.steps: OPTIONS, 'How much is out there' set to Lean (its own hint promises it moves 'What everything is WORTH, including the stash you have already banked'). At Wirt, press Gamble $2,500 and roll, say, a Data Core. The history row under THE GAMBLE reads '$520'. Hover the same Data Core in the stash: '$364 each'; Sell one pays $364 and 364 XP. Rich shows the reverse ($520 in the log, $702 everywhere else). Every other price surface, the stash hover, the tag-junk hint, the Peddler panel, the shelf line at the Mainframe, prints ival(); this is the one row on the raw val.
confirmed.test: Inside the closure, after __resetCfg: var _k=CFG.lootMult; CFG.lootMult=0.7; var _g=P.gambleLog; P.gambleLog=['core']; renderGamble(); var t=document.querySelector('#gamblelist .vl').textContent; then restore CFG.lootMult=_k, P.gambleLog=_g, renderGamble(). Assert t==='$'+ival('core').toLocaleString() with lootMult 0.7 (expects '$364'; current build prints '$520'). Control: the same read with CFG.lootMult=1 gives '$520' on both builds.

verdict.reason: Confirmed in C:\claudecode\dark raiders\dark_raiders.html. renderGamble (line 31611) prints each history row with `''+'$'+it.val.toLocaleString()+''` (line 31622), where `it=ITEMS[log[i]]` — the raw table value. ival (line 1773) is `Math.round((ITEMS[k]?ITEMS[k].val:0)*CFG.lootMult)`, and the OPTIONS row 'How much is out there' (line 37494) sets lootMult Rich 1.35 / Standard 1 / Lean 0.7 (lines 37501-37503); its v8.75 comment states lootMult is read inside ival() and moves what the banked stash sells for. Data Core val is 520 (line 1964), so Lean gives round(520*0.7)=364 and Rich 702, exactly the quoted numbers. Every sibling price surface goes through ival(): stash hover `'$'+ival(k).toLocaleString()+' each'` (32718), tag-junk hint (32150), Sell one `P.credits+=ival(k); P.xp+=ival(k)` (32795), Peddler pedPrice (9312) and panel (27468), Mainframe shelf line `ival('core')` (30825), stash canvas hint (28300). The gamble history is the only display that reads .val directly (the only other `.val.toLocaleString` at 27267 is a raid-log entry object, not ITEMS). No comment near 31622 or in the gamble button handler (35991-36000) or the v15.03-v15.05 wirt-audit notes declares the raw value deliberate; the v15.05 comment directly below concerns only the button's comma. Display-only: at Standard the output is identical, and the value credited on sale is already ival(), so no dial moves. The row is not a TXSHIP key. The proposed fix is correct and in scope: `log` and `i` are live at that line (31616-31619) and ival returns a rounded number, so `.toLocaleString()` is safe.

confirmed.title: The mercenary death line says 'you are in debt' before the run's own money has landed
confirmed.code: P.credits-=MERC_DEATH; lines.push(''+mname+' died. Death benefit '+'$'+MERC_DEATH.toLocaleString()+' owed'+(P.credits<0?', you are in debt':'')+'.');
confirmed.steps: Hire someone and go up holding, say, $1,000 banked. He dies. Sell about $5,500 of loot at the Peddler ($3,000 rides with you) and extract. The card's hire line reads '<name> died. Death benefit $3,400 owed, you are in debt.' while the same card's money line and the Undercroft show $600 banked: the clause is decided at 1,000-3,400 = -2,400, before the stall money (line ~20438) and hazard pay (line ~20392) are added further down the same function. Only rack pay lands before it. The clause can only ever be wrong in this direction (says debt when there is none).
confirmed.test: Inside the closure on the fixture: stage a raid, P.merc=IDENTITIES[0].id, G.mercDead=1, P.credits=1000, G.bag=[], G.carriedIn=0, G.pedCarry=G.pedSold=3000, P.terms=[], call endRaid('extract'), read document.getElementById('oc_manifest').innerHTML. Assert it contains 'Death benefit' and NOT 'you are in debt' while P.credits===600; the current build prints 'you are in debt' beside a positive balance. Control: same staging with G.pedCarry=0 ends at P.credits===-2400 and must contain 'you are in debt' on both builds. Restore the profile snapshot through the loader in finally.

verdict.reason: Confirmed in C:\claudecode\dark raiders\dark_raiders.html. Inside endRaid (starts at 20126) the only credit that lands before the merc settle is rack pay, `P.credits+=_mfPay;` at 20248 (extract only). The merc block then does `P.credits-=MERC_DEATH;` at 20270 and on the very next line (20271) decides the clause from the running balance: `' owed'+(P.credits<0?', you are in debt':'')`. Two extract-only credits land further down the same function: hazard pay `P.credits+=bonus;` at 20392 (bonus = Math.round(Math.max(0,haul-(G.carriedIn||0))*tPay), guarded by how==='extract'&&tPay>0) and stall money `if(G.pedCarry&&!G.sim){ P.credits+=G.pedCarry; }` at 20438 inside the how==='extract' branch. Stall money is genuinely not banked at the sale: pedSell does `G.pedCarry=(G.pedCarry||0)+tot;` at 9532 under the v7.62 comment "stall money is CARRIED, not banked ... nothing touches P until the extract branch" (9529-9531). No other P.credits write exists between 20271 and the end of endRaid (grep of P.credits shows none between 20438 and 27497; bankItem at 20083 and contractExtract at 3355 do not touch credits). So with $1,000 banked, a dead hire and $3,000 riding on pedCarry, the line prints 'you are in debt' at -2,400 while the extraction settles at $600 (the Undercroft header at 32479 reads the final P.credits). On dead/abandon nothing lands after 20271, so the clause is only ever wrong on an extraction, and only in the debt-when-none direction. Not balance (no number moves, only the clause condition), not deliberate (the nearby comment at 20240-20242 only says a bad merc run can put you in debt), and 'Death benefit ... you are in debt' is not a TXSHIP key (the sentence exists only at 20271). The proposed fix is exact and correct: `haul` is in scope from 20149, termsPay() (19791) is pure and equals the tPay computed at 20326, the pedCarry and hazard terms reproduce 20438 and 20391-20392 exactly (both zero when absent), G.sim is already excluded by the enclosing `if(P.merc&&!G.sim)` at 20264, and `_mdIn` is unused elsewhere in the file.

confirmed.title: A restore code neither carries nor clears the imported friend
confirmed.where: restoreMake() object literal (about line 33305-33319, the cc: line) and restoreApply() (about line 33406, the 'rest the code does not carry' line)
confirmed.code:
cc:P.cdone||0,   // v15.01, save audit finding 2: the contracts he completed, beside the standing it already carries
  P.merc=null; P.contracts=[]; P.seals={}; P.mapSeen={}; P.discover={}; P.terms=[]; P.notExt=0;
confirmed.steps: 1. In the Mainframe, type a name and IMPORT A FRIEND with a run report; the hint reads '<name> walks your raids: ...'. 2. Settings, Recorder: paste a RESTORE CODE made by a character who never imported anyone, READ CODE, type restore. The panel says it REPLACES the save you are playing. 3. Open the Mainframe: it still says '<name> walks your raids', and applyGhost still re-dresses a pillager as that friend on the restored character's raids. The reverse also fails: a code made from a character WITH a friend, applied on a fresh browser, comes up with no friend and the import prompt, and the report file is needed again. restoreApply already clears the hire, contracts, seals, kit, Wirt's lot and explored maps for exactly this reason (v13.61, v14.04, v15.00-v15.02); P.ghost is the one row of the Mainframe it never touches, and restoreMake never writes it.
confirmed.fix:
cc:P.cdone||0,   // v15.01, save audit finding 2: the contracts he completed, beside the standing it already carries
         gh:(P.ghost&&typeof P.ghost==='object'&&P.ghost.tag)?P.ghost:null,   // the imported friend (applyGhost reads P.ghost)
  P.merc=null; P.contracts=[]; P.seals={}; P.mapSeen={}; P.discover={}; P.terms=[]; P.notExt=0;
  P.ghost=(o.gh&&typeof o.gh==='object'&&typeof o.gh.tag==='string'&&o.gh.tag)?o.gh:null;   // the code's friend, or none: never the replaced character's

Then P.ghost={tag:'OLDONE',wep:'pistol',wepName:null,runs:1,ext:0,rate:0,avgHaul:0}; make code2 with P.ghost temporarily null; restoreApply(restoreRead(code2)); ARM B asserts P.ghost===null (current build: OLDONE survives, fails). CONTROL: after each apply, P.credits===restoreRead(code).c and P.rivals deep-equals its rv, which passes on both builds and proves the code round-trips; only the gh field changes between builds.
confirmed.summary: restoreApply never carries or clears P.ghost, so a restored character inherits or silently loses the imported friend.

verdict.reason: Confirmed every step in the current file. (1) P.ghost is written in exactly one place, importGhost at line 30729 `P.ghost=g;`, and is never cleared or nulled anywhere (grep for `P.ghost=`, `ghost=null`, `delete P.ghost` finds only that line). (2) restoreMake (33304-33335) writes keys v,n,c,x,l,r,e,d,b,no,pk,ra,ar,cs,sc,ki,cb,j,mi,cd,wq,ne,rv,cc,w,s,g and nothing for the ghost; the quoted `cc:P.cdone||0,` line is at 33318. (3) restoreApply (33363-33427) sets or clears every other Mainframe/character row (P.intel=0 at 33403, the quoted `P.merc=null; P.contracts=[]; ...` line at 33406, P.freeKit/wirtLotBought at 33409) and never touches P.ghost, then calls saveProfile() at 33425, which stores JSON.stringify(P) whole (line 2669), so the replaced character's ghost object is written into the restored save. (4) The code path reloads (38267-38269) and applyLoadedProfile sets P=d from that storage, so the ghost survives; applyGhost() is called on every raid build at 10963 and reads P.ghost.tag/wep/rate (30743-30764), and renderMainframe prints `P.ghost.tag+' walks your raids: '` at 30819-30820. The reverse (a code from a character with a friend applied on a fresh browser) has no key to read, so P.ghost stays undefined and the import prompt shows. The panel sentence at 1164 promises the code REPLACES the save. The finishRestore comment (37602-37608) says the backup file and UNDO paths replace the whole profile, so only the code path leaks. No comment or ruling in the file, memory or handoff notes says the friend is deliberately browser-local; the v14.04 "rest the code does not carry" list simply missed it. Not balance: no number moves, and the fix touches no player text or TXSHIP key. The proposed fix is correct and complete: the `gh:` entry slots into the object literal before `w:{},s:{}`, the `P.ghost=` line after 33406 takes the code's friend or null (an older code with no gh clears the replaced character's friend, matching the v15.00 rivals rule), and applyGhost already guards WEAPONS[P.ghost.wep].

confirmed.title: Killing the friend's ghost twice makes it your rival on paper, and no pillager can ever be marked rival again
confirmed.where: myRival() (about line 9137-9144); its only consumer is mkRaider's rival: field (about line 9219)
confirmed.code:
for(var id in (P.rivals||{})){
    var r=P.rivals[id],f=(r.kills||0);   // v13.94: kills alone. deaths is only ever a hire dying on your job.
confirmed.steps: 1. Import a friend. 2. In two raids, shoot and kill the ghost (the kill at the death path writes idRec('ghost_<name>').kills++ each time, so the record reaches 2, then 3). 3. From then on myRival() returns 'ghost_<name>' whenever that count beats every real identity (the strict f>bs needs only 2), and mkRaider's rival:(ident.id===myRival()) can never match because no IDENTITIES id begins 'ghost_' and applyGhost only re-dresses a body after the roll. Result the player sees: the star on the pillager board vanishes, the 'YOUR RIVAL is out here: <name>. He will shoot on sight.' line never plays, G.tel.rivalMet is never set and rivalMet:1 drops out of the run report. A player who had a rival at 2 kills loses him the moment the ghost's count passes it, and gets him back only by out-killing his own friend.
confirmed.test: Inside the closure, with P.rivals saved and put back in finally: var real=IDENTITIES[0].id; P.rivals={}; P.rivals[real]={kills:2,deaths:0,met:2,standing:-2}; P.rivals['ghost_ZQX']={kills:3,deaths:0,met:3,standing:-3}; ARM A asserts myRival()===real (current build returns 'ghost_ZQX', fails). CONTROL: P.rivals={}; P.rivals[real]={kills:2,deaths:0,met:2,standing:-2}; asserts myRival()===real, which passes on both builds. Optional world arm: with arm A's records, G=buildRaid(false) for a seed where IDENTITIES[0] spawns and count G.ents.filter(function(e){return e.rival;}).length; 0 today, 1 with the fix; G=null afterwards.
confirmed.summary: myRival() can return the ghost's ledger key, which no IDENTITIES entry ever equals, so the rival system goes dark.

verdict.reason: Every step holds in the current code. applyGhost (line 30751: e.ident='ghost_'+String(P.ghost.tag).slice(0,24); e.rival=0;) re-keys the ghost's body after buildRaid, called at line 10963 after the roster was rolled. Player rounds land on a friendlyPC raider (bullet loop 19464-19512 has no friendly pass-through; only mercs are skipped) and a killing round sets en.byPlayer=true (19549). The death path (17759-17761: if(e.kind==='raider'&&e.ident&&!G.sim){ var rr2=idRec(e.ident); rr2.kills++; ...}) has no ghost guard, so P.rivals['ghost_<tag>'].kills climbs; the same write exists on the linked-window path (35867-35868). rivalsForCode (33296-33300) carries any non-zero record through a restore code, so the ghost record persists. myRival (9137-9144) walks every key of P.rivals with a strict f>bs from bs=1, so two kills on the ghost make 'ghost_<tag>' the answer whenever it ties or beats no real identity's count (strictly greater than each). Its only consumer is mkRaider line 9219 rival:(!simBuild&&ident.id===myRival())?1:0, and ident only ever comes from IDENTITIES (9090-9131, no id starts with 'ghost_') or the suffixed clones at 10532-10534 and 15316, so no body can match and rival is 0 for everyone. Downstream: the 'YOUR RIVAL is out here' line and G.tel.rivalMet (10978-10983) never fire, the star on the board (27163) vanishes. No comment or ruling covers this: the v13.93 note at 30749 only says the ghost's ledger writes must land on him, and the v13.94 note at 9140 only removes deaths from the score. Not balance; no numbers move. The proposed fix (skip 'ghost_' keys inside myRival's loop) is the right place, since the v13.93 comment wants the kill written on the ghost's own record, so the exclusion belongs in the chooser, not the ledger.

confirmed.title: The ghost's own ledger is written but never read: 'will remember that' is said and nothing remembers
confirmed.where: applyGhost() (about line 30751-30752); writers at the raider death path (about 17759-17763), the revive (about 16392-16396) and the friendly-shot flip (about 18506-18509)
confirmed.steps: 1. Import a friend. 2. Kill the ghost in a raid: the game says '<name> will remember that.' and writes kills 1, standing -2 on P.rivals['ghost_<name>'] (v13.93 keyed the ledger to the ghost 'so the writes land on him'). 3. Next raid: mkRaider rolls grudge/hostile/standing from the BODY's own identity record, then applyGhost sets hostile=false, friendlyPC=1, grudge=false unconditionally and never opens the ghost's record. The friend walks up with the [FRIENDLY] plate and 'nods at you' or 'is watching you' by the body's standing, not his. The same holds for the revive's '<name> is back on his feet. He will remember that.' (+3 standing that nothing reads). By the feature's own rule, 'friendly the way a parleyed raider is friendly', a parleyed man you killed is shoot-on-sight next run. This is his call: if the friend should stay friendly whatever you do, the fix is instead to skip the two 'will remember that' lines when e.ghost is set.
confirmed.test: Inside the closure, profile snapshotted and restored in finally: P.ghost={tag:'ZQXFRIEND',wep:'pistol',wepName:'Scav Pistol',runs:4,ext:1,rate:25,avgHaul:0}; P.rivals=P.rivals||{}; P.rivals['ghost_ZQXFRIEND']={kills:1,deaths:0,met:1,standing:-2}; G=buildRaid(false); applyGhost(); var g=G.ents.filter(function(e){return e.ghost;})[0]; ARM A asserts g&&g.grudge===true&&g.hostile===true&&!g.friendlyPC (current build: friendlyPC 1, grudge false, fails). CONTROL: delete P.rivals['ghost_ZQXFRIEND']; G=buildRaid(false); applyGhost(); the ghost has friendlyPC===1 and grudge===false on both builds. G=null after each arm.
confirmed.summary: applyGhost forces the ghost friendly every raid and never reads the ghost_ record that killing, shooting or reviving him writes.

verdict.reason: Confirmed in the current file. applyGhost (30742-30768) sets `e.ident='ghost_'+String(P.ghost.tag).slice(0,24); e.rival=0;` then `e.hostile=false; e.friendlyPC=1; e.grudge=false;` unconditionally and never calls idRec(e.ident); e.standing is left as mkRaider set it at 9241 (`grudge:rec.kills>0, standing:rec.standing`) from `rec=idRec(ident.id)` at 9188, i.e. the BODY's record. The three writers all key on e.ident and so land on P.rivals['ghost_<tag>']: the death path 17758-17763 (`var rr2=idRec(e.ident); rr2.kills++; rr2.standing=Math.min(rr2.standing-2,-1); rr2.met++; ... sayWhenFree(e.name+' will remember that.')`, plus the same in netKillTake 35867-35870), the revive 16392-16396 (`rrv.standing=(rrv.standing||0)+3; rrv.met++; ... say(downRdr.name+' is back on his feet. He will remember that.')`), and the parley betrayal 18506-18509 (`rb.standing=Math.min((rb.standing||0)-3,-1)`). The only readers of P.rivals are idRec (9132), myRival (9137, kills only) and rivalsForCode (33296, export); mkRaider only ever looks up IDENTITIES ids, and 'ghost_' appears nowhere else in the file, so nothing feeds the ghost's record back into the ghost. Next raid he is rebuilt friendly with the [FRIENDLY] plate (23985 reads friendlyPC) and 18522 says 'nods at you'/'is watching you' from the body's e.standing. Not deliberate: the v3.83 rule (DESIGN.md 13663-13676) is 'Friendly the way a parleyed raider is friendly', and a parleyed man is shoot-on-sight after a kill (mkRaider 9248 `hostile:(rec.kills>0)?true:...`, parley refusal at 8053 on e.grudge); the v13.93 comment at 30749 and p1393.ps1 only aimed to stop the stranger's record being blamed, and both DESIGN.md (v13.93 section) and AUDIT.md line 1709 record 'Not verified: reviving or betraying the ghost'. Nothing after applyGhost() at 10963 re-flips him (kit tick 15142, crowd count 15541 and sim pick 16846 all skip e.ghost). Not balance, no TXSHIP key reworded, no retired word. The proposed fix is correct: idRec is live-only here (applyGhost bails on G.sim), the empty record it creates is dropped by rivalsForCode, e.standing then drives 18522 from the ghost's own ledger, and kills>0 gives the same grudge/hostile pair mkRaider gives any identity. It is his call whether a betrayal without a kill (standing -3, kills 0) should also carry over; the fix as written leaves him friendly but 'watching you', which matches mkRaider's treatment of negative standing without a kill closely enough. Side note for a separate finding: myRival (9137-9143) does count the ghost's kills, and 'ghost_<tag>' can never equal an IDENTITIES id at 9219, so a ghost killed more often than any pillager makes the rival star go to nobody.

confirmed.title: A NIGHT raid is labelled with a daylight hour on the CONDITIONS row and the sector map, and the map header names the new weather on both sides of the arrow for the second half of every turn
confirmed.where: drawHUD, CONDITIONS panel IIFE, about line 25372; drawMapOverlay, about line 28432

The CONDITIONS row top-right reads 'noon   Clear' (or '8am   Foggy', 'DAWN   Storming', '6pm ...') for the whole raid; open the sector map and its right-hand header says the same. verdict.reason: Both halves confirmed in the current code. Half one: TODS (lines 5693-5699) holds only DAWN/8am/noon/6pm/8pm and pickTod (5749-5767) picks from it with no look at P.cond; buildRaid stores it as `tod:pickTod(WX_ROLL)` (10822) and tod() (5700) returns it. The sector NIGHT button sets P.cond='night' (36755) and isDay() is `P.cond==='day'` (7060). Every visual reader of the hour is gated on isDay(): the cast `if(isDay()&&TD.add)` / `if(isDay()&&TD.dim)` (24320, 24326), the lamps `wx().lights*(isDay()?tod().lights:1)` (24256, 23264, 24340, 16042). But the two labels are not gated: the CONDITIONS row `rows.push({k:MT.name+'   '+MW.name,...` with `MT=tod()` (25349, 25372) and the map header `ctx.fillText(tod().name+'  '+wx().name+` (28432). So a NIGHT raid prints 'noon   Clear' or '8am   Foggy' with no NIGHT anywhere on the HUD. Nothing declares this deliberate: the TODS comment ('Every entry is DAYLIGHT') predates the v9.97 sector-page NIGHT choice, and the run record already treats night as a separate fact from the hour (`night:(...!isDay())?1:0`, 20749, 'his answer 22: the record knows it went up in the dark'). Half two: wx() returns wxMix(G.wx,G.wxNext,G.wxT) while a turn is running (5526); wxMix sets `WXBLEND.name=(t<0.5?a.name:b.name)` (5521); WX_TURN=14 (5531), so from 7s after the 'The weather is turning.' say (5579) the header prints the destination name on both sides of the arrow ('Storming  → Storming  71%'). The CONDITIONS panel reads MW=(G.wx||WEATHER[0]) (25349), i.e. the origin, so the two surfaces also disagree with each other during that window. The proposed fix is correct and complete: G.wx.name is safe because G is only ever built by buildRaid (10943, 20928), which always sets wx (10811), and drawMapOverlay runs only from the raid HUD (26595). 'NIGHT' matches the sector page vocabulary (959, 36015) and no TXSHIP sentence is touched. Not balance. Out of scope but noted: the rain and fog alpha at 24560 and 24582 read tod().lights without the isDay() gate, so at night a noon roll gives full-strength rain, the opposite of the comment's intent.

Line 5700 `function tod(){ return (G&&G.tod)||TODS[2]; }` and line 10822 `tod:pickTod(WX_ROLL),` set the hour once per raid; pickTod (5749-5767) draws `TODS[ri(0,TODS.length-1)]` uniformly from all five entries with no P.cond gate, and only re-lands golden under storm/blackout, so a RAIN night raid rolls 8am or noon (both `lights:0`, lines 5695-5696) two times in five. Line 7060 `function isDay(){ return P.cond==='day'; }` is the night switch; nothing overrides G.tod at night (no `G.tod=` anywhere). Line 24560 `var _rl=(typeof tod==='function'&&tod())?tod().lights:0;` feeds `(0.20+_rr*0.09)*(1-0.45*_rl)` at 24561, and line 24582 `var _fl=(typeof tod==='function'&&tod())?tod().lights:0;` feeds `_fa=_fg*(1-0.40*_fl)` at 24583; neither asks isDay(). Every other live reader of tod().lights is gated: 24256 `fk*=wx().lights*(isDay()?tod().lights:1);`, 16042, 23264, 24340, and lampBase (5787-5792) `if(!d) return 1;` whose comment at 5785-5786 states the design: "at night the lamps are the light", i.e. the darkness figure at night is 1. The rain block's own comment (24554-24559) says the alpha should be "full strength at noon, a bit over half in the dead of night" and calls tod().lights "the darkness figure", which is only true under isDay(); the TODS header (5686-5687) says "Every entry is DAYLIGHT", so the night surface added later inherited an ungated read. The night sheet (24240-24242, NIGHT_SHEET up to .82) is blitted onto wc at 24304 `wc.drawImage(litC,0,0);` BEFORE the rain (24561) and fog (24584) draw, so the sheet does not darken them; on a noon-hour night they draw at 0.29 (rain=1) over the darkest scene the game has, and at 0.16 on an 8pm-hour night. Not balance (a render alpha), no ruling or comment makes it deliberate, and the hour tint at 24320 is already gated `if(isDay()&&TD.add)`. One correction to the auditor's framing: the hour is not fully hidden, the conditions box at 25372 (`rows.push({k:MT.name+'   '+MW.name,...`) and map overlay at 28432 print tod().name at night too, but that does not change the fault. The proposed fix is correct; isDay is a hoisted global already called in this pass (24240, 24314, 24320). Equivalent and using the one named helper: `var _rl=lampBase();` / `var _fl=lampBase();` (returns 1 at night, tod().lights by day).

G.lightning is set only at 5624 (the bolt) and read only in render2D: 24415 fog lift, 24644 countdown, 24647/24650 flash; WX/W2.lightning readers are 5519 (wxMix), 5595 (strikeTick), 24645 (render), 25371 (row); G.strikes is read only by strikeTick and the ring draw at 24610. The sight rules (18164 wkSight, 18177 _fSee=_far0*(alert?1.35:1)*pcon*wkSight, 18188 canSee, 18232 crouch past CHID 170, 18234 downed) read nothing storm-related, and canSee at 7970 does not either. The bolt ping at 5627 is ping(S.x,S.y,900,false,false,'env','fire'): machines within 900*wx().noise of the STRIKE point (180-800 from the player, 5602-5604) go alert and investigate S.x,S.y (12983-12986), not the player. So in the stated scenario the sentry stays idle through every flash: the text lies. Not deliberate: the comment at 24648-24649 and DESIGN.md 395 state the intent 'you to anything looking', and the v6.87 entry (DESIGN.md 25577-25600) claims it 'cuts both ways' but only lifted the fog sheet, which hides things from the player alone; no ruling says machines should not see you in a flash. Also confirmed: render2D never runs headless (runSim 20931 -> simStep 20903-20919 has no countdown), so the proposed mechanic without the simStep line would hold G.lightning at 0.34 after the first sim bolt. Neither string is a TXSHIP key (table at 2362 carries 'Storming. Harder going, so XP pays 1.1x.' and not these), and no check or fixture greps them (only backups/). HOWEVER the proposed primary fix is the wrong default: writing the mechanic is a design and feel change (RULEBOOK rule 1: balance numbers, design changes, anything he may dislike the feel of -> ask; memory: no balancing before alpha), and as written it has no distance cap (any machine with a clear line across a 5200x4000 world, facing any way, sees you), ignores e.blind (18164) and ignores the cone the 24648 comment names ('anything looking'). The provable, ship-without-asking fix is the words (RULEBOOK: 'wrong text I can prove'), with the mechanic parked as a question for him.

verdict.reason: Confirmed in the current code. Raid start: `wxTurnsLeft:(rr()<0.30?2:1)` (10815) and `wx:(WX_ROLL=pickWeather())` (10811). pickWeather (5774-5780) rolls `rollTable([['clear',26],['partly',16],...])` with no exclusion of partly; wxTick's only rejection is `while(nw.id===G.wx.id&&guard++<12) nw=pickWeather();` (5555). The rain-or-storm override is gated on the CURRENT sky, `if(G.wx&&G.wx.id==='partly'){` (5559), so a turn INTO partly is never redirected. Then `G.wxNext=nw; G.wxT=0;` (5573), `G.wxTurnsLeft--;` (5574) takes the count from 1 to 0, and `say('The weather is turning. '+nw.line)` (5579) prints the partly entry's `line:'Partly cloudy. This will not hold.'` (5490). After WX_TURN the blend completes, `if(G.wxT>=1){ G.wx=G.wxNext; G.wxNext=null; G.wxT=0; }` (5536), and every later frame exits at `if(G.wxTurnsLeft<=0) return;` (5539). wxTurnsLeft is written nowhere else (grep: 5539, 5553, 5574, 10815 only), and the partly entry's `turns:1` field at 5489 is declared but read by nothing, so no other mechanism forces the promised break. The sector comment at 962-965 states partly "is the one state that exists to TURN into another", and the v6.67 comment (5556-5558) says the break "actually tells you something" on reading it, so a partly sky that holds to extraction contradicts both the spoken line and the stated design. This is a state-machine contradiction, not a dial. The proposed fix traces correctly: after `G.wxTurnsLeft--` the guard re-arms one turn only when nw is partly; the next expiry hits 5559 and can only yield rain or storm, which is not partly, so the count then falls to 0 and stays there (no loop); the pinned path returns at 5553 before reaching it, and partly is unreachable by pin (no button at 966-974). Optional tidier form that makes the dead table field live: `if(nw.turns&&G.wxTurnsLeft<nw.turns) G.wxTurnsLeft=nw.turns;` but the proposed line is correct as written.
